prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: production transparent animation spritesheet for a Windows desktop companion.
Primary request: create an original small BLUE WHALE business desktop mascot, in understated premium contemporary consumer-electronics industrial design reminiscent of Apple product design, with a mild science-fiction character. This is a real whale animal, NOT a girl or human character. Rounded compact streamlined whale body, ceramic satin blue upper shell, pearl-white underside, restrained silver fin rims, two small refined dark eyes, a tiny subtle cyan indicator detail; a calm, competent and approachable expression. Clean seamless surfaces, soft studio highlights, crisp edges, three-quarter orthographic 3D render. No logos, no Apple logo, no typography, no accessories unless explicitly specified below.
Output: EXACTLY 4 columns by 9 rows, 36 individual full-body transparent sprites, regular equal-sized cells, entire canvas 1536 x 2304 pixels, each cell 384 x 256. NO margins between cells, NO labels, NO grid lines. Every whale stays within its own cell with generous transparent padding. Similar body scale in every cell, pivot and center consistent, tail and fins fully visible, no cutoffs. True alpha transparency, no floor, background, ground shadows or environment.
Each row is a smooth FOUR-FRAME sequence left to right:
ROW 1 idle: whale faces front-right, almost motionless hovering, tiny breathing and fin drift, eyes mostly open.
ROW 2 running-right: swims horizontally toward screen RIGHT, body tilts right, four alternating tail and fin beats, expression focused, short clean cyan motion streak behind whale.
ROW 3 running-left: swims toward screen LEFT, exact same identity and scale, four tail and fin beats, cyan motion streak behind whale.
ROW 4 waving: friendly professional greeting, faces front-right, ONE front fin raises outward then gently waves for four poses, other fin stays attached.
ROW 5 jumping: modest success celebration, anticipation then short rising leap then crest then relaxed landing; small cyan sparkle at crest only.
ROW 6 failed: calm concern, subtle amber status ring near the fin and slightly lowered head, four restrained poses; no crying or comical distress.
ROW 7 waiting: attentive holding pose, gazes toward a small floating hollow cyan dot beside its front fin, gently varying fin/eye pose.
ROW 8 running (command execution): focused operation, holds one small transparent cyan console slab beside a fin, four successive slight fin gestures, NO text on console.
ROW 9 review: reviewing results, a small silver transparent data card beside a fin and attentive head tilt, four slight scan/head changes, NO text.
Constraints: single identical original whale mascot throughout all 36 cells, two fins, one tail, consistent eye placement, consistent palette/material/light and body proportions. Suitable for screen sharing in business meetings: sophisticated, minimal, quiet. No costumes, no childish stickers, no human hands, no human anatomy.

Use case: background-extraction
Asset type: transparent desktop animation spritesheet.
Edit the supplied blue whale spritesheet. Remove ONLY its entire blue-gray studio gradient background and the floor/ambient background, making those pixels genuinely fully transparent with an alpha channel. KEEP ALL 36 whale sprites and their fins, tails, ceramic materials, highlights, silver rims, cyan indicator details, cyan streaks, status rings, sparkles and translucent data cards unchanged. Preserve exact same image dimensions, EXACT 4-column 9-row regular grid, positions and scale of every sprite. The result is a production RGBA sprite atlas, no backdrop, no checkerboard pattern printed in the pixels. Keep clean antialiased edges, no blue background patches around transparent effects. Do not redesign the whale, do not move frames, do not add or remove frame details.
